key_insight: Apparent progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization (MMDG) is often driven by inconsistent evaluation protocols; a standardized, comprehensive benchmark reveals which gains are real and which are artifacts.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmentation and lack of standard evaluation in MMDG research—inconsistent datasets, modality setups, and metrics have made it unclear whether reported improvements reflect true algorithmic advances.
method: Assemble a comprehensive benchmark spanning multiple datasets, tasks, and modality configurations (beyond action recognition) to increase coverage and realism.
Define and enforce unified evaluation protocols (fixed splits, preprocessing, modality ablations, and common metrics) and re-evaluate prior MMDG methods under these standards.
Perform systematic analyses (ablation and sensitivity studies) to identify which factors drive reported gains and where real robustness improvements occur.
impact: Provides a single, fair yardstick for comparing MMDG methods, improving reproducibility and helping practitioners identify genuinely robust approaches that generalize across modalities and domains.
visual_elements: Bar chart: reported performance vs. standardized-benchmark performance for several prior MMDG methods to show over-/under-estimation.
Dataset–Modality matrix heatmap showing coverage gaps and which tasks/modalities the benchmark includes.
Flowchart of the standardized evaluation protocol (data splits → preprocessing → modality regimes → metrics).
Radar chart comparing algorithm robustness across multiple target domains/modalities after re-evaluation.
paper_title: Are We Making Progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization? A Comprehensive Benchmark Study
paper_authors: Hao Dong, Hongzhao Li, Shupan Li, Muhammad Haris Khan, Eleni Chatzi
